symptom: Orchestrator's step 2 (planning) emitted zero output tokens. System prompt cached (cache.read: 11905) and input tokens arrived (input: 463), but the model emitted nothing.
root_cause: google/gemini-2.5-flash silently returns zero-output on long-system-prompt + tool-calls reasoning shapes. The orchestrator's planning step triggered this limit.
fix_applied: Batch 20: switched orchestrator to openrouter/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 to route around Gemini Flash's zero-output behavior.
reproduction: Set orchestrator model to google/gemini-2.5-flash, run the smoke test, observe step 2 with output tokens = 0 across retries.

symptom: When OpenCode's Anthropic provider SDK was invoked for claude-sonnet-4-6, it hit /messages instead of /v1/messages and returned 404.
root_cause: The Anthropic provider config had no baseURL, so the SDK path suffix /messages concatenated to https://api.anthropic.com/messages instead of https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages.
fix_applied: Batch 21: added baseURL: https://api.anthropic.com/v1 to provider.anthropic.options so the suffix resolves correctly.
reproduction: Remove baseURL from provider.anthropic.options, request any Anthropic model directly via the SDK, observe 404 on /messages.

symptom: Every step's response metadata showed google.thoughtSignature, even though the orchestrator was configured for anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6 (via OpenRouter proxy, then direct Anthropic).
root_cause: Initially misdiagnosed as OpenRouter misrouting. Actual cause (Finding O, batch 17d): claude-sonnet-4-6 has no dated snapshot in OpenCode's model registry. When the ID can't be resolved, OpenCode silently falls back to small_model (google/gemini-2.5-flash). Both batches 20 (OpenRouter) and 21 (direct Anthropic) silently landed on Gemini.
fix_applied: Batch 22 (pending): set opencode.json top-level model to a verified-working Sonnet ID (candidates: claude-sonnet-4-5, claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929).
reproduction: Set opencode.json model to any unresolved alias. Run any mission. Inspect response metadata for google.thoughtSignature; if present, fallback is active.

symptom: Edit tool call failed with string-not-found on oldString the model believed was in the file.
root_cause: Model included Read's `4: ` line-number display prefix in oldString instead of the raw file content.
fix_applied: Mission retried with corrected oldString (prefix stripped); succeeded on second try.
reproduction: Read a file, then compose an Edit using the Read output verbatim as oldString. The `N: ` prefix will not match actual file bytes.

symptom: Agent called a tool named `isoformat` which does not exist in its manifest.
root_cause: Model synthesized a tool name from intent (needed an ISO timestamp) instead of using an existing tool. The manifest had no datetime utility, so the model invented one.
fix_applied: Mission fell back to a hardcoded midnight value. Future fix: use Bash with `date -Iseconds` or similar.
reproduction: Give the agent a task requiring a current timestamp while omitting any datetime tool from the manifest. Model may invent a tool name.

symptom: Smoke-test mission ran 2h17m between some steps; total runtime blew the 30-minute budget.
root_cause: OpenRouter's free-tier Gemini rate limiting (secondary effect of the Finding L silent fallback — orchestrator was actually calling Gemini via OpenRouter, hitting aggressive throttles).
fix_applied: Batch 21 removed OpenRouter from the orchestrator path (direct Anthropic). Batch 22 (pending) fixes the underlying model-ID resolution so Gemini isn't being called at all.
reproduction: Route orchestrator through OpenRouter free-tier Gemini at high request volume; expect inter-step latency spikes.

symptom: First smoke-test attempt failed at preflight STOP CONDITION 1 — dirty tree, missing dev deps, no tests directory. Orchestrator never invoked.
root_cause: Not strictly a consult skip — more a preflight skip. Recording here as 'consult-skipped' because the broader lesson is that preflight is a first-class consult and must be treated as such in future tiers.
fix_applied: Batch 18 installed ruff/pytest, created requirements-dev.txt, added the missing test directory structure.
reproduction: Run batch 17 preflight on a clean checkout with no dev deps installed; expect STOP CONDITION 1 to fire.

symptom: TIER-CLASSIFIER rule 1 misfired: request 'migrate LCN storage backend to postgres' classified as MVP instead of Enterprise. Unit test caught it before the classifier shipped.
root_cause: First implementation used substring match `kw in text.lower()` over a tuple of bare keyword strings ('migrate', 'rewrite', 'architecture', ...). Morphological variants like 'migration' bypassed 'migrate', and 'architectural' bypassed 'architecture'. The Convention 'verify a model ID resolves' has an analogue here — 'verify rule fires on the morphology you actually see in requests, not just the lemma.'
fix_applied: Replaced ENTERPRISE_KEYWORDS tuple-of-strings with ENTERPRISE_PATTERNS tuple of compiled regex with stem variants and word boundaries: r'\bmigrat(e|es|ed|ing|ion|ions)\b' etc. Added regression test 'emigration stats' confirming word boundaries prevent false positives. Helper _contains_enterprise_keyword rewritten to iterate patterns and return human-readable label.
reproduction: Set ENTERPRISE_KEYWORDS = ('migrate',) and call classify('migrate storage backend', [...], 50). Returns MVP instead of Enterprise because substring 'migrate' matches but morphological equivalents ('migration', 'migrating') don't.
